messages:
Marta (Design): Quick UX note: when the filters bottom-sheet opens on small phones, it pushes the compact table header up and the sticky filter pills overlap the first row. Repro on 320px width.
Evan (Product): Screenshot? Is it consistently reproducible?
Marta (Design): Yep, consistent on iPhone SE and older Androids. Screenshot: https://img.redwood/mock/filters-bottomsheet-overlap.png
Noor (Frontend): Likely due to bottom-sheet using translateY but not updating the sticky offset. We set header top via JS based on toolbar height, but the sheet changes layout after paint.
Ken (Mobile): In WebView the keyboard + sheet combination is worse. The sheet triggers a reflow and the header calc runs before the final height.
Marta (Design): UX wants to avoid the overlap. Options: 1) reserve extra bottom spacing when sheet opens; 2) move filter pills into the sheet on narrow widths; 3) make sheet modal and dim content so overlap is less confusing.
Noor (Frontend): Pragmatic approach: when sheet opens on <=360px move inline filter pills into the sheet and set a short transition buffer before recalculating sticky offsets. CSS: `.filters-inline { display: none; } .filters-in-sheet { display: block; }` JS: delay 60ms after animation end before measure.
Ken (Mobile): For WebView add a11y: ensure the sheet gets focus and the background is inert. Use `inert` polyfill for older Android WebViews. Also test focus trap.
Evan (Product): Makes sense. Prefer moving pills into sheet on tiny screens to avoid hitting sticky calculations. Keep primary CTA visible.
Marta (Design): Copy tweak: label the sheet header "Filters & view" and the collapse affordance "Close filters". Keep the sheet close button accessible and big.
Noor (Frontend): I'll prototype: move pills into sheet at <=360px, add 60ms post-transition measure, and ensure `aria-hidden` on background. Will open PR and link ticket RDC-1612.
UX-Bot: Automated note: created RDC-1612 "Bottom-sheet filters - overlap with compact header on narrow screens" and linked this thread.
Ken (Mobile): I'll test on Android WebView + iOS WKWebView and report any quirks.
Marta (Design): Thanks all ":thumbsup:" — ping when PR is up and I'll verify spacing and hit targets.
